original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.

original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

actual_scope: Sharp relative coefficient and worst basis-pair output error for a shared phase-weighted Fourier convolution routine with nonzero order-two read translation.
scope_change_reason: Originally posed quantitative approximation question at a Fourier boundary; this is a precision/analytic side result, not a selected caller or active-mode injection construction.
bottleneck_link: A proposed approximate producer/consumer Fourier contract cannot have arbitrarily small relative error under the shared translated interface. Physical costs and selected supplier budgets remain unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop at the first verified sharp error floor and attaining weights; do not extend to other orders, norms or physical callers.
evidence: PROOF.md gives the all-group argument; verify.py gives exact field, polynomial, literal Fourier, coefficient/moment and rejecting-control evidence with source-bound generated receipts.
